summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes and a history of gastroparesis was admitted for a flare of nausea and vomiting. She was kept NPO initially, given IV fluids, and treated with anti-nausea medications including Ativan and Zofran. Her blood pressure, which was elevated at admission, normalized as her nausea improved. She gradually advanced to a regular diet, remained asymptomatic, and was discharged home in stable condition. No new medications were added, but she was advised to taper her Ativan to avoid withdrawal. Follow-up was arranged with her PCP and gastroenterologist for ongoing management of hypertension and gastroparesis.
problems: Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type I [juvenile type], uncontrolled
